# Building Trabzonspor's AI Analysis Room

## Welcome

It is Saturday night. Tomorrow, Trabzonspor play Gaziantep FK at home. You are the new AI analysis
staff of the club. The coaches want a match briefing by the morning.

In this tutorial, you build the staff from agents with Google's **Agent Development Kit (ADK)**.
Each step adds one staff member, and each staff member is one agent pattern. All agents use real
data from the last ten matches of both teams.

![The whole staff](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/overview.svg)

[Open the diagram full size](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/overview.svg)

| Step | Pattern | Staff member |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `LlmAgent` with tools | The Scout |
| 2 | `SequentialAgent` | Match Prep |
| 3 | `ParallelAgent` in a `SequentialAgent` | Scouting Department |
| 4 | `LoopAgent` | Tribün |
| 5 | Orchestrator with `AgentTool` | Technical Director |

In each step, the key code is missing. A one-line ✏️ BLANK marker is in its place. The tutorial
selects the BLANK line for you. You paste the code over it, save, and run the step.

You need a Google Cloud project with billing. Free trial credits work. The agents call Gemini
through Vertex AI in your project. The guide has the full explanations and the diagrams:
[omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/).

<walkthrough-tutorial-duration duration="60"></walkthrough-tutorial-duration>

## Set up

Select a project that has billing. The agents call Gemini through Vertex AI in this project.

<walkthrough-project-setup billing="true"></walkthrough-project-setup>

1. Set this project in Cloud Shell:
   ```bash
   gcloud config set project <walkthrough-project-id/>
   ```
   If Cloud Shell asks you to authorize gcloud, click **Authorize**.
2. Run the setup script (about 1 minute):
   ```bash
   bash scripts/setup.sh
   ```
   It checks the project and its billing, turns on the Vertex AI API, installs the Python
   packages, and writes <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath=".env">.env</walkthrough-editor-open-file>. Read the script: <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="scripts/setup.sh">scripts/setup.sh</walkthrough-editor-open-file>.
3. Start the ADK dev UI:
   ```bash
   uv run adk web --reload_agents --port 8080 --allow_origins "*" steps
   ```
   With `--reload_agents`, the dev UI loads a file again when you save it. With
   `--allow_origins "*"`, the Web Preview page can connect to the dev UI.
4. Click <walkthrough-web-preview-icon></walkthrough-web-preview-icon> **Web preview**. Then
   click **Preview on port 8080**. The dev UI opens in a new tab.
5. Click **+** in the terminal to open a second tab. Use it for all other commands. The dev UI
   continues to run in the first tab.

✅ **Check:** the script ends with `✅ Ready`. The dropdown at the top left of the dev UI shows six
apps, from `bonus_live_mcp` to `step5_technical_director`. Until you fill a step, the terminal
shows `✏️ BLANK ... paste its code over this line` when you select it.

## The data and the tools

All agents use a snapshot from FotMob, ESPN and Turkish match reports (30 October 2026):

- <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="data/README.md">data/README.md</walkthrough-editor-open-file>: what each file contains, and the stories in the data.
- <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="data/squad.json">data/squad.json</walkthrough-editor-open-file> and <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="data/opponent.json">data/opponent.json</walkthrough-editor-open-file>: the two squads, with the
  availability of each player for Sunday and the statistics of the last ten matches.
- <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="data/match.json">data/match.json</walkthrough-editor-open-file>: the fixture, the referee, the coaches and the head-to-head.

The agents never read these files. They call tools:

- <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="matchday/tools.py">matchday/tools.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>: the 11 tools. Python does all the calculations: **LLMs
  interpret, tools count.** `null` in the data becomes `"not available"`, never zero.
- <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="matchday/config.py">matchday/config.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>: the model and the house rules. Every agent answers in the
  language of the user. Write in Turkish, and the agents answer in Turkish.

## Step 1 · The Scout

One `LlmAgent` has an instruction and tools. The instruction tells the agent who it is and how to
work. The tools are Python functions that the agent can call.

![Step 1: the scout](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/step1-scout.svg)

[Open the diagram full size](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/step1-scout.svg)

### ✏️ BLANK 1 · the whole agent

**Copy the code.** Click the copy button at the top right of the code below. The
[guide](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/step-1/#blank-1) explains each line.

```python
def build_scout(
    name: str = "scout",
    description: str = "Looks up players and team form: stats, availability, top performers, recent results.",
    tools: list | None = None,
) -> LlmAgent:
    return LlmAgent(
        name=name,
        model=MODEL,
        description=description,
        instruction="""
You are the scout on Trabzonspor's analysis staff. "We" and "us" always mean Trabzonspor.
Answer questions about players and teams.

How you work:
1. Look everything up with your tools before you answer. Never answer from memory.
2. "In form" means recent output and ratings: check top players by goals, assists and avg_rating.
3. "Who can't play" means the availability list: out and doubtful players with the reason.
4. Name the player, then the numbers that back up your point.
""" + HOUSE_RULES,
        tools=tools or SCOUT_TOOLS,
    )


root_agent = build_scout()
```

**Select the blank.** Click <walkthrough-editor-select-regex filePath="steps/step1_scout/agent.py" regex="[ ]*raise NotImplementedError\(.{1,6}BLANK 1 · .*">BLANK 1 in steps/step1_scout/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-select-regex>. The editor opens the file and selects the BLANK line.

**Paste and save.** Press Ctrl+V (⌘V on a Mac) to replace the BLANK line. Then press Ctrl+S (⌘S) to save.

### Run it

In the dev UI, select `step1_scout`. Then send this question:

```text
Who's in form for us, and who can't play Sunday?
```

✅ **Check:** the events panel shows calls to `get_top_players` and `get_availability`. The answer
gives 8 goals and 5 assists for Salah, and the players who are out or doubtful.

**Late?** In your second terminal tab, run this command. It pastes the code for you:

```bash
uv run python scripts/blanks.py fill 1
```

## Step 2 · Match Prep

A `SequentialAgent` runs its sub-agents in a fixed order. Each sub-agent saves its answer with
`output_key`. The next sub-agent reads it with a `{placeholder}` in its instruction. Open
<walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="steps/step2_match_prep/agent.py">steps/step2_match_prep/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>: the opponent analyst and the lineup picker are
already there. You add the tactician and the line that connects the three agents.

![Step 2: match prep](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/step2-match-prep.svg)

[Open the diagram full size](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/step2-match-prep.svg)

```python
        name="tactician",
        model=MODEL,
        instruction="""
You are Trabzonspor's tactician. Opponent report from the analyst:
{opponent_report}

Check our own form with get_team_trends("Trabzonspor"), then write a game plan:
formation, how we attack, how we defend, and what to do in each phase of the match.
""" + HOUSE_RULES,
        tools=[get_team_trends, get_match_info],
        output_key="game_plan",
    )
```

## Step 3 · Scouting Department

A `ParallelAgent` starts three scouts at the same time. Each scout writes its own state key. Then
a report writer merges the three reports. Open
<walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="steps/step3_scouting_dept/agent.py">steps/step3_scouting_dept/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>: the three scouts are already there.

![Step 3: scouting department](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/step3-scouting-dept.svg)

[Open the diagram full size](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/step3-scouting-dept.svg)

### ✏️ BLANK 3 · the report writer

**Copy the code.** Click the copy button at the top right of the code below. The
[guide](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/step-3/#blank-3) explains each line.

```python
    report_writer = LlmAgent(
        name="report_writer",
        model=MODEL,
        instruction="""Merge three scouting reports into one brief for Trabzonspor's coaches.
Attack report: {attack_report}
Defense report: {defense_report}
Discipline report: {discipline_report}
Write four short sections: Threats, Weaknesses to attack, Discipline and referee, Three key takeaways.
Use only facts from the reports; if they disagree, say so.""" + HOUSE_RULES,
        output_key="scouting_brief",
    )
    scouts = ParallelAgent(name="scouts", sub_agents=[attack_scout, defense_scout, discipline_scout])
    return SequentialAgent(name=name, description=description, sub_agents=[scouts, report_writer])
```

## Step 4 · Tribün

A `LoopAgent` runs a lineup picker and a critic again and again. The critic is the Tribün, the home
crowd. When it agrees with the lineup, it calls `exit_loop`. `max_iterations=3` is the safety
limit. Open <walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="steps/step4_tribun/agent.py">steps/step4_tribun/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>: the lineup picker is already there. Its
instruction reads `{tribun_feedback?}`. With the `?`, round one can start without feedback.

![Step 4: the Tribün loop](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/step4-tribun.svg)

[Open the diagram full size](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/step4-tribun.svg)

### ✏️ BLANK 4 · the Tribün

**Copy the code.** Click the copy button at the top right of the code below. The
[guide](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/step-4/#blank-4) explains each line.

```python
    tribun = LlmAgent(
        name="tribun",
        model=MODEL,
        instruction="""
You are the Tribün: Trabzonspor's passionate home crowd. Loud, funny, loyal, never rude.
Criticise choices, not people. Cheer for us; never chant against the opponent or its fans.

The proposed lineup:
{lineup}

Check it with your tools; do not trust the numbers in the proposal.
1. Out players are rejected. Doubtful players need a named, available backup.
2. If our home record is strong, demand attacking intent.
3. Flag card-risk players (red cards or many yellows) and ask for a plan for them.

If all three checks pass, call exit_loop, then cheer the approved XI in two lines.
Otherwise reply with numbered objections, each with the number that proves it.
Don't invent new demands each round: approve as soon as the checks pass.
""" + HOUSE_RULES,
        tools=[get_availability, get_player, get_team_trends, get_discipline, exit_loop],
        output_key="tribun_feedback",
    )
    return LoopAgent(name=name, description=description, sub_agents=[lineup_picker, tribun], max_iterations=3)
```

**Select the blank.** Click <walkthrough-editor-select-regex filePath="steps/step4_tribun/agent.py" regex="[ ]*raise NotImplementedError\(.{1,6}BLANK 4 · .*">BLANK 4 in steps/step4_tribun/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-select-regex>. The editor opens the file and selects the BLANK line.

**Paste and save.** Press Ctrl+V (⌘V on a Mac) to replace the BLANK line. Then press Ctrl+S (⌘S) to save.

### Run it

In the dev UI, select `step4_tribun`. Then send this question:

```text
Pick the XI for Sunday.
```

✅ **Check:** the Tribün objects in round one, with numbers from its tools. The lineup picker fixes

## Step 5 · Technical Director

An orchestrator is an `LlmAgent` that has other agents as tools. Each team from steps 1 to 4 is in
an `AgentTool`. The director selects a team by its **description**. Open
<walkthrough-editor-open-file filePath="steps/step5_technical_director/agent.py">steps/step5_technical_director/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-open-file>.

![Step 5: the technical director](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/step5-technical-director.svg)

[Open the diagram full size](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/diagrams/step5-technical-director.svg)

### ✏️ BLANK 5a · the descriptions

**Copy the code.** Click the copy button at the top right of the code below. The
[guide](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/step-5/#blank-5a) explains each line.

```python
# Delegation is driven by these descriptions: they are all the director knows about each team.
SCOUT = "Answers questions about ONE player or ONE team: form, minutes, goals, ratings, availability."
MATCH_PREP = "Writes Sunday's game plan: opponent analysis, then tactics, then an XI of available players."
SCOUTING_DEPT = "Full scouting report on Sunday's opponent: threats, weaknesses, cards and the referee."
TRIBUN = "Picks a final XI and has the home crowd stress-test it. Only when asked to pick or defend the XI."
# Try it live: uncomment these, ask the same questions again, and watch the routing go wrong.
# SCOUT = "Helps with football."
# SCOUTING_DEPT = "Also helps with football."
```

**Select the blank.** Click <walkthrough-editor-select-regex filePath="steps/step5_technical_director/agent.py" regex="[ ]*raise NotImplementedError\(.{1,6}BLANK 5a · .*">BLANK 5a in steps/step5_technical_director/agent.py</walkthrough-editor-select-regex>. The editor opens the file and selects the BLANK line.

**Paste and save.** Press Ctrl+V (⌘V on a Mac) to replace the BLANK line. Then press Ctrl+S (⌘S) to save.

### ✏️ BLANK 5b · the teams

**Copy the code.** Click the copy button at the top right of the code below. The
[guide](https://omarcevi.dev/workshops/match-day-agents/step-5/#blank-5b) explains each line.

```python
    # Each team becomes a tool: the director calls it like a function and gets its answer back.
    teams = [
        AgentTool(build_scout(description=SCOUT)),
        AgentTool(build_match_prep(description=MATCH_PREP)),
        AgentTool(build_scouting_department(description=SCOUTING_DEPT)),
        AgentTool(build_tribun(description=TRIBUN)),
    ]
```
